Basavaraja, J., Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

The appellant/petitioner has preferred this appeal against the judgment and award dated 13.07.2017 passed in MVC.No.1692/2014 on the file of the Court of the VIII Additional District and Sessions Judge, Belagavi (hereinafter referred to as the 'Tribunal').
2. The parties are referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal, for the sake of convenience.
3. Factual matrix of the case in brief are on the evening of April 6, 2012, the petitioner was heading home on his motorcycle with registration number KA-22/EJ-346 NC: 2023:KHC-D:9241-DB after completing his day's work in Belagavi.

entities.text: VIII Additional District and Sessions Judge, Belagavi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: He was traveling along VTU Road, nearing the campus on VTU Santi-Bastwad double road, at approximately 9:30 PM.

At this point, a Jeep with registration number KA-22/G-282 approached from the opposite direction, driving recklessly on the wrong side at high speed, disregarding traffic rules, and endangering human lives.
Tragically, the Jeep collided with the petitioner's motorcycle, resulting in severe injuries.

sentences.text: The petitioner incurred substantial medical expenses, totaling over Rs.4,00,000, for his treatment and recovery.
Regrettably, due to the injuries sustained in the accident, the petitioner had to undergo the amputation of his right leg, leading to permanent and total physical disability.
Consequently, he lost his capacity to earn a livelihood.

Prior to the accident, the petitioner worked as a mason, earning a monthly income of Rs.10,000/-.
5.

In light of these circumstances, the petitioner holds respondent Nos.1 and 2, who are the owner and NC: 2023:KHC-D:9241-DB driver of the involved Jeep, as well as respondent No.4, the insurer of the Jeep, responsible for providing the necessary compensation.
The petitioner earnestly requests the acceptance of this claim petition.
appeared through learned ADGP and respondent No.3 appeared through its counsel.
7. Respondent Nos.1 and 3 submitted their statements of objection, refuting all the allegations presented in the claim petition and requested dismissal of the said petition.

8. In view of the above pleadings, the Tribunal has framed the following issues:
"1. Whether petitioner proves that he has sustained injuries in an accident occurred on 06-04-2012 at 21- 30 hours at Campus, double road, VTU Santi-Bastwad, Belagavi due to rash and negligent driving of Jeep bearing No. KA-22/G-282 by its driver?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
What order?"
9. To support the petitioner's case, three witnesses were presented, namely PWs1 to PW3, and a total of 250 documents were marked as Exs.P1 to P250.

Subsequently, in defense of the respondents' position, respondent No.2 testified as RW1 and introduced three documents marked as Exs.R1 to R3.
10.
Upon a meticulous study of all the evidence and materials presented, the Tribunal issued its judgment and award dated 13.07.2017.

In this judgment, it granted compensation amounting to Rs.
19,35,187/-.

However, the Tribunal attributed 50% contributory negligence to the petitioner,
resulting in respondent No.4 being held responsible for paying only 50% of the compensation,
which amounts to Rs. 9,67,593/-.
Furthermore, interest at a rate of 9% per annum was awarded from the date of the petition until full realization.
Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, the appellant/claimant has preferred this appeal.

Heard Sri. Ashok A.Naik, learned counsel for the appellant/claimant, Sri. S.M.Muchandi,
learned counsel for respondent No.2, Sri. S.K.Kayakamath, learned counsel for respondent No.3 and Sri. Praveen Uppar, learned HCGP for respondent Nos.1 and 4.
SUBMISSIONS ON BEHALF OF THE APPELLANT 13.
The learned counsel representing the appellant/claimant has presented arguments challenging the judgment and award issued by the Tribunal.

Their main contentions are as follows:
13.1.
The Tribunal made a significant error by attributing 50% contributory negligence to the appellant.
They claim that there is documentary evidence to establish that the Jeep involved in the accident belonged to the Police Department.

A charge sheet was filed against the appellant merely as a means to evade responsibility, and it NC: 2023:KHC-D:9241-DB was alleged that a false story had been concocted by the police authorities concerning the accident.

In an attempt to refute these allegations, the appellant filed a private complaint against the police, and the Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC) Court in Belagavi issued summons to the driver of the police Jeep.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC) Court in Belagavi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The driver challenged this order by filing Revision Petition No. 259/2015 before the I Addl. District & Sessions Judge, Belagavi.

entities.text: I Addl. District & Sessions Judge, Belagavi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The appellate court dismissed the revision petition, thereby supporting the appellant's position.
All relevant documents were presented to the Tribunal to disprove the charges against the appellant.
Nevertheless, the Tribunal, without proper consideration, incorrectly concluded that the appellant also contributed to the accident.
This conclusion is erroneous and should be set aside.

13.2. It is further submitted that the Tribunal awarded compensation for loss of future earnings based on a monthly salary of Rs.7,500/-, which the appellant believes is lower than the actual income of Rs.10,000/-
NC: 2023:KHC-D:9241-DB per month earned through masonry and tile-fitting work.

Additionally,
the appellant contends that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal for other aspects is also inadequate.
In light of these arguments, the appellant requests that the appeal be allowed.
SUBMISSIONS ON BEHALF OF THE RESPONDENTS 14.

Learned counsel appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.2 & 3 and learned HCGP for respondent Nos.1 & 4 submit their arguments that the Tribunal has appreciated the evidence on record in accordance with law and facts and there are no grounds to interfere with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal and sought for dismissal of the appeal.

15. Having heard the arguments on both sides, and on perusal of the records, the following points would arise for our consideration:

16.Our answer to the above points are as follows:
Point No.1 - Partly in the affirmative Point No.2 - as per the final order REASONS 17.

The Tribunal in paragraphs 8 to 22 of its judgment, has discussed the evidence on record and fixed the liability of the petitioner to the extent of 50% negligent and remaining 50% on the driver of the Jeep.
18. The Tribunal has observed that PW1 has specifically stated that the accident as occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the Jeep bearing Regn.No.KA-22/G-282.
It is also observed that the charge sheet has been filed against the petitioner as per Ex.P8 and the petitioner has been acquitted in the said case in C.C.No.500/2012 by order dated 18.01.2014.
The - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:9241-DB complainant/victim/State has not preferred any appeal against the judgment of the acquittal in CC.No.500/2012 which was registered against the petitioner.

The Tribunal has also observed that the present petitioner has filed a private complaint in P.C.No.166/2013 on the file of the JMFC II Court, Belagavi, cognizance is also taken against respondent No.2 and case was registered in C.C.No.267/2013.

Being aggrieved by this order passed by the JMFC II Court, the revision petition was filed by respondent No.2 i.e., the driver of the offending vehicle against the order of cognizance taken in C.C.No.267/2013 in Revision Petition No.250/2015, same was dismissed by the District Court.
The respondents have not placed any material as to the result of C.C.No.267/2013 on the file of the JMFC II Court, Belagavi.

On reappreciation/re- evaluation of evidence on record, we are of the opinion that the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the Jeep bearing Regn.No.KA-22/G-282.
- 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:9241-DB 19.

The Tribunal has taken the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.7,500/- per month by relying on the decision of this Court in the case of KALLAPPA Vs. ABDUL SHOAIB SHAIKH AND ANOTHER reported in 2017 ACJ 297 (Karnataka).

As per the decision of the Apex Court in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED V. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, 40% is to be added towards future prospects.
